thread.title: Fitbit stock heads for best day ever as Citron praises health opportunity

author: Emily Bary
title: Fitbit stock heads for best day ever as Citron praises health opportunity
text:
Investors appear to be betting that Fitbit Inc. is ready for a comeback, sending shares to their highest levels since early 2017 on Monday.
The wearable-technology company has suffered the past two years, losing more than 80% of its post-IPO valuation amid competition from Apple Inc. and difficulties breaking into new markets. Shares have been climbing steadily higher for the past two weeks, however, and took off Monday in a record-breaking rise.
The stock was up more than 18% in Monday afternoon trading, which would be Fitbit’s FIT, +16.46% largest single-day percentage gain in history. The rally started early in the day, after the company announced that its kids’ wearable device, the Fitbit Ace, was now globally available for sale . Shares received a bigger jolt around midday, when short-selling specialist Citron Research made a bullish call , arguing that Fitbit’s stock could more than double by year-end—if the company doesn’t first get acquired—thanks to its health care initiatives.

“What was once a piñata for short sellers (since IPO) has transformed itself to one of the most underappreciated med-tech stories in the market with a balance sheet and brand equity that gives investors a tremendous investing opportunity,” Citron analysts wrote in a report Monday.
Among the areas of interest for Citron are Fitbit’s glucose-monitoring partnership with DexCom Inc. DXCM, +2.09% employee-wellness partnership with insurer UnitedHealthcare, and cloud partnership with Alphabet Inc.’s GOOGL, +1.07% Google. That last arrangement makes the Citron team believe that Google could be considering a takeover soon.
“Beyond their partnership, Google will likely integrate the Fitbit data and become the default platform for every non-Apple Watch wearable,” wrote the Citron analysts, who value the stock at $15. “Think Android for watches.”
Much of the enthusiasm on Fitbit of late stems from belief that the company’s core hardware business will eventually rebound, as well as the nascent opportunities in health technology. Fitbit’s health-solutions business, though, remains unproven. The company’s outgoing chief financial officer told MarketWatch after Fitbit’s latest earnings release that health solutions remain “still a relatively small portion of our revenue stream today.”
The company’s device business, which Citron called “dead,” has shown some recent momentum. The company disclosed a week ago that it’s sold more than a million Versa smartwatches since the product became widely available in mid-April, making the Versa Fitbit’s fastest-selling product in history . That statistic helped lift Fitbit shares in every trading day last week, even as the company’s CFO announced his plans to leave the company and Apple AAPL, -0.20% announced new Apple Watch features during its WWDC keynote.

Fitbit’s stock is up 35% so far this month, compared with a 3% gain for the S&P 500 SPX, +0.31% , but it’s still trading more than 60% below its $20 IPO price and far below its all-time high of $51.64.
Emily Bary Emily Bary is a MarketWatch reporter based in New York.
